---
title: Returns policy
department: customer-support
status: current
---
Northwind handles returns on behalf of merchant customers. The merchant sets the
commercial terms; Northwind sets the operational ones, and the two are often
confused by consumers contacting support directly.

A consumer initiates a return through the merchant, never through Northwind. A
consumer who contacts Northwind is directed back to the merchant, because
Northwind has no visibility of whether the merchant has accepted the return.

Once a merchant authorises a return, a return label is generated and is valid for
twenty eight days. An expired label cannot be reactivated; the merchant issues a
new one. Labels are valid for a single parcel and a second parcel presented on
the same label is refused at the drop off point.

Returns travel on the Standard Ground tier regardless of the tier used for the
outbound shipment. A merchant who wants faster return transit buys a return
service explicitly, and this is a common source of a perceived delay when a
consumer expects the return to move as quickly as the delivery did.

Drop off points accept returns during their own opening hours, which are not the
same as depot hours. A parcel dropped off after the daily collection moves on the
next collection, which adds a transit day.

A return is scanned at the merchant's returns facility, not at a Northwind depot,
so Northwind tracking ends at the facility door. Support agents should set that
expectation clearly, since the gap between the final Northwind scan and the
merchant's refund is where most consumer complaints originate.

Damaged returns are photographed at the drop off point and the images are
attached to the tracking record. Where a consumer disputes the condition of a
returned item the images are the evidence both parties rely on.
